review:
[b]Pros[/b]
-The sniping mechanics are really good. The game takes into account bullet drop, wind, stance (whether you are crouching, laying down or standing), breath and motion.
-The game lets you tackle a level the way you want to. You are only given a waypoint and how you reach that waypoint is up to you.
-The levels are fairly open. Most levels have several big “arenas” connected by corridors.
-The A.I can be quite challenging...

[b]Cons[/b]
-The A.I can also be very dumb at times. I saw a couple of times enemies just giving up and resuming their normal route right after they had spotted me or I had killed someone next to them
-Some minor bugs
-At times the enemy can spot you behind cover or behind boxes which can be frustrating when you have successfully sneaked past several enemies.

[b]Neutral[/b]
-Rebellion has been updating the game with “advertising” for their other Sniper Elite games. Now at the start of the game there is a launcher that is just one advert for their newer game and when closing the game there is another advert that you have to manually quit.


I found Sniper Elite V2 to be quite an enjoyable experience. The gameplay is good and can accommodate any type of player (whether you run and gun, use stealth or anything in between), the story while not being anything remarkable is enjoyable and the mission structure is good enough to keep you playing. Sniper Elite is a fun game and an easy one to recommend.

Sniper Elite V2 is a solid arcade shooter. These days everyone expects ultra realistic sims which, honestly, barely exist even from big AAA studios but this game never pretends to be one. Yes, some moments are noticeably scripted, but it’s still a fun, satisfying shoot ’em-up. It’s not all sniping, either. Movement can feel a bit clunky at times, and the machine gun takes some getting used to, but the levels are interesting, the visuals are good, and the kill cam is always entertaining. The game is surprisingly addictive, blending sneaking, fast action, and some light planning. On Normal and higher difficulties it can put up a fight, but it’s definitely manageable. One odd design choice is that levels must be completed in one sitting if you make it through several checkpoints and quit, you’ll be starting over from the beginning next time. Not sure why they went with that, especially since most people don’t have unlimited free time. Still, I can see myself replaying levels just for fun. Sniper Elite V2 might not be everyone’s cup of tea, but if you enjoy shooters third person movement with first person aiming you’ll likely have a good time. Just don’t expect it to be something it isn’t. If you just want a fun, well-made arcade sniping experience, this is worth a try.

This is one of my favourite games, I played the Demo back on PS3 and then bought the game back when it came out. I played the Nazi Zombie Army games then a few years later and I really enjoyed them too. Playing through V2 again, this christmas has been great and it has reminded me how much fun this game is to play. 

This is the definitive sniper game, in my opinion and the addition of the surreal anatomical, slow motion, skeletal, destruction just makes it even cooler. In fact, Rebellion has made a great impression on me as an awesome developer with both this game and their spin-off zombie mode. The Nazi Zombie Army trilogy are also really well designed, original and super fun.

The sniping gameplay in Sniper Elite V2 is really enjoyable and the developers do a great job mixing things up and keeping it interesting. There are stealth sections too and the automatic weapons have a nice punch to them. Some people complain online about the close range weapons being too underpowered. I think these weapons feel great, your character can’t take too much damage but neither can your enemies. So these encounters are very satisfying because a well placed headshot from a weaker gun will do the job. While some of the more powerful variants will destroy an enemy at close range. 

In regards to the guns, they have included a well designed and cleverly presented selection of weapons. With each weapon feeling like it has its own unique characteristics and authentic details. Varied gameplay elements can force you to change up your approach to sniping and there is nice selection of guns to choose from to get you through.

The DLC is really worth getting too as it differentiates itself from the main campaign with it’s new locations. Each of these DLC missions take place in gorgeous environments that are really fun to play through. The developers also continue there surreal brilliance with the assassinate the Fuhrer mission. This is so cool and I noticed that it’s become a repeated theme throughout the series. 

I just replayed this game after buying it in the christmas sale and I also bought the rest of the series. I’m excited to try Sniper Elite 3 and 4 to see how the series has progressed and especially to see how Rebellion have developed their slow motion skeletons.

Disclaimer: I've played through this game years ago, and loved it. This review is based on my feelings upon playing it just now on Steam.

The sniping sections? Great, mostly! Pulling off crazy, difficult shots, wiping out entire armies before any of them know what hit 'em, and seeing your plan come to fruition feel brilliant. If it was just for those sections, I'd absolutely recommend this game.

Unfortunately, this game, which has SNIPER right there in the name I'll remind you, has only a handful of actual sniping sections. Most of the single player campaign is spent with stealhy 3rd person action sequences. Levels usually start off with you just behind enemy lines, armed with a sniper rifle, SMG with barely any ammunation, and a sidearm; the only remotely useful of which is the silenced pistol. You have a few grenades, some mines/traps and binoculars, the usefulness of which I cannot fathom, seeing as how your main weapon has a freakin' scope.

From there you're expected to make your way through hordes of enemies to an arbitrarily chosen sniping spot, snipe out a few waves of enemies, and make your escape. In theory, you can stay far away from your enemies and use your sniper effectively all through the levels. In reality, you're constantly forced into tight corridors and indoors areas, where the game devolves into a run-and-gun action game, and a very mediocre action game at that.

You cannot climb anything(aside from the pre-determined sniping sections), so you can't use verticality to your advantage. This means you often have to walk into large outdoors areas trying to look at every direction and every height at once. There are far too many ledges, windows and rooftops for you to clear, while also keeping an eye on the ground. And even if you do clear them all, the enemies move from one place to another, so a window being empty right now might not be empty in ten seconds.

Oh, yeah, and enemy snipers sometimes spawn seemingly out of thin air. There's a mission towards the end where you're forced to make your way through a narrow road, when suddenly enemies spawn both behind you and in front of you. So while you're trying to fight off the enemies coming from both sides, you'll notice a sniper has spawned on a rooftop to the side of you -- a rooftop you'll likely have cleared by that point.

And if that's not enough to get the salt flowing, the enemies also blatantly cheat, the snipers being the worst offenders. Not only do they have the high ground, having just spawned there (in locations you simply cannot reach), they also have perfect aim and perfect reflexes. Once the enemies know your location, you can't peek your head out without getting shot. It is literally impossible to shoot and enemy before they shoot you, if they know your location. And changing locations doesn't make much of a difference, since the enemy snipers often see you instantly, even if you're in a spot that should in theory be outside of their field of view -- or at least unfavorable for them. They also don't care about minor things like smoke, fire or trees, and they'll see you through all of those obstacles, even if you have no chance of seeing them.

The game is honestly not about planning, scouting, using the terrain to your advantage, aim, reflexes or smarts. It's about trial and error. There is simply no way for you to avoid getting shot at the first time you're playing the maps. You'll have to learn the enemy locations by heart and abuse the game mechanics (using the 3rd person view to look around corners for example) to stand a chance against the masses of enemies and superhuman counter snipers; and even then, you'll often get swamped by hordes of enemies coming from every angle and height, so the game devolves into you camping behind a corner with a SMG, shooting moronic enemies who run into your sights.

There's a mission in which you are expected to clear out some elite Russian snipers that are camping in buildings around a courtyard ("Exfiltrate through the rooftops"). This mission shows this game at it's most frustrating, and I had to stop playing for a long time because this mission made me want to tear out my own eyes. Not only do the enemies spawn at arbitrary times at arbitrary locations, all of which you'll have to memorize through trial and error, the enemies NEVER miss any shots and react instantly to you peeking out from behind a corner. If all this isn't bad enough, some enemies can hit you from behind cover; the only cover you're given, mind you, so the only way to complete the mission is to bait the enemy AI into missing, then taking out the snipers one by one, pausing after each one to let your health go back up, because you die in two hits and each sniper WILL get at least that one shot in, regardless of how well you play. This section in particular is HORRIBLE game design, and a great showing of all of this games flaws.

So it's not a sniping game, which is a shame, since the sniping sections are really enjoyable; just too few and too far apart for me to recommend this game. You simply don't have the tools or means to make stealth viable, and I don't buy games with SNIPER in the name for half-assed run-and-gun action gameplay. 

A ton of wasted potential, and FAR less enjoyable than what I remembered. Sadly.

I actually have been playing this series in an odd order. I completed SE3 first, then SE1 (Wasn't into it with it first came out, but recently became fond of it, probably after seeing what they did to it with V2 and 3), and now am wading through SE2. I liked SE3 quite a bit, it was a lot of fun, but my main gripe with it was the braindead AI and broken stealth mechanics. Which still exists here. But the upside was that SE2 was a bit more of a playground, and the AI were slightly more aggressive.

So in Sniper Elite V2, you obviously play as a sniper, but you don't really feel like one at all. It just feels like it's on rails to me. Most often, the best thing to do when you see enemies is to just sit and one spot and shoot all of them. Yeah, even with the difficulty and realism settings on max. You don't even have to be good at it, honestly, just wait for your health to come back and pop out to rapid-fire snipe them until it hits them. Though there is a lot of reward to get headshots and vital shots without the diamond aim assist. With the aim assist you just get to feel badass.

But sitting in one place for five minutes is bad, right? No, the AI (even at the highest difficulty) don't really do anything that forces you to move. You never need to set up traps like they show you in the tutorial, you'll barely get any good chances to use them. They lack the ability to perform fire-and-movement tactics, or flanking maneuvers, and grenades are easily dealt with by walking backwards. Just inch your gun out from behind cover to where nobody can shoot you, but you can shoot them. That's it. If they get too close you can just use iron sights on your rifle, or throw a grenade (they won't run away from them). All of the submachine guns are worthless (you're more likely to die using them than you are killing anyone with them). I haven't tried any pistol except for the Welrod, with its gloriously inaccurate 6-round magazine, so if they are any good I am unaware of it. Welrod is nice though. Even if you fail the miserable stealth system, just shoot them three times in a row with the welrod to kill, and no matter how much yelling they make, it won't attract anyone. It just stunlocks them. Actually, it doesn't seem like ANYTHING the AI says influences their fellow soldiers. Their speech is just empty, like only you can hear it.

Speaking of stealth, it's simple. Don't be seen, don't be heard. Well, often times falling a short distance (maybe a foot off of some object, this is a normal thing when proceeding through the level) will cause some horrendous noise that alerts enemies half a block away from you, causing them all to walk around awkwardly shouting "I know you're here, sniper!!" "Sniper no sniping!!" "What was that!? A sniper?!". Yet shooting someone that is just a foot away from someone facing the opposite direction, having them scream and gasp and fall to the ground, will not alert them...this is exactly the problem I had experienced in SE3, and I get this crap in almost every level.

Another thing, which is kind of interesting, is that there are some environmental noises that can mask your gunshot. But..it doesn't really make sense. Your gunshot is only masked if YOU are in range of the object that masks your noise. An enemy could be by a noise source and hear everything going on. But if you stand by a noise source and a bullet whizzes right past their face, they aren't going to notice a thing. Nope. Not even if it hits the wall right beside them.

One time, I think it was the third level, in the underground factory or whatever it was, I had a big firefight on one of the big hallways. Of course all I had to do was crouch behind a table and shoot all six of those nazis. Despite all of their hollering and return fire, I walk into one of the side corridors, not even 10 meters away from a dead nazi, and there's a guy just peacefully walking along as if he didn't notice a thing.


So basically, I don't know what anyone was expecting from these sequels. But I was coming to this hoping for an awesome, gritty, realistic, stealth-sniping game, and if you want that you can give SE1 a try, it's not great but it's good (really dated, might not be an issue for other gamers). What I got was more like a light gun shooter. This game could've been great, but everything about how the AI reacts to the player made it go all wrong. SE3 is better, but still has the same problems. And I'll probably get SE4 too just because it's supposed to be even more sandboxy.

First time I write a review here, so I might as well write it proper.

As I see it, Sniper Elite falls between a number of chairs. It tries to have it's cake and eat it too, and suffers greatly due to it. It's part stealth, part action and long range focused. Problem is, there is no good way of planning attacks, the gameplay is linear and the sheer number of enemies makes this game in a much poorer condition than it could have been in.

The offset is pretty good. There aren't alot of games that focuses on the role of the sniper/marksman out there, and so far nobody has really suceded in recreating that aspect of combat. The game tries to come off as realistic, having it's balistic model as one of it's most adverticed selling points. And to some extent, the bullet physics are great, exept bullets can't penetrate anything, even a wooden fence can stop these bullets. Only thing it actually does penetrate are foilage and bodyparts... the latter it doess rather well.

The levels of the game does not invite the player to plan their attacks, as I stated earlier. In addition, there is far to much focus on close quarters combat for this to really take the art of sniping seriously. Snipers and marksmen are mainly covert operators, and they are usually only used for high value target and recon, not as the one man army portrayed in this game. The gameplay is repetative, unintuitive and plain booring in the long run, and it's far from as interesting as it could have been.

It does, however, provide some entertainment if you have nothing else to do for 30 minutes, but as a game to sit down and enjoy for an evening, it doesn't serve at all.

Hope that you'll find this review helpful, comments are welcome.

I picked this up on Steam in the "collection" version when it was on sale for a bit under $20. I've only been playing this for twenty-some odd hours now, but I really like it. I find myself replaying missions over and over chasing that perfect run, and trying out different tactics. Last night I played a mission pretty cleanly, and didn't get shot once so I got the "Hide and Hope" achievement. It felt like I had actually accomplished something! 

This game has reminded me of how much I like stealth mechanics, and slow, tactical gameplay. Now I've ordered other similar games for my library that I never played for some reason (Hitman series, Splintercell series). In fact, even though I'm less than half way through this campaign (and haven't played any of the coop), I went ahead and got Sniper Elite 3 and its season pass (together for $35, thanks internet!).

The gameplay is very deliberate, if you like a run-n-gun style, this won't work for you. I really appreciate the tension and atmospherics in this game. Often even when I know I can safely run in a section, I will choose not to just because I hate making so much noise. 

Your sniper rifle is your best weapon. Your secondary has very limited range and accuracy, and also limited ammo on the battlefield (though there are strategies to improve this). You have to think like a sniper, don't shoot from a window, shoot from deep within the room, from the shadows (bonus, increased distance points!). Pulling off a perfect mission takes patience and strategy. Pulling it off with style takes experimentation and creativity (I pulled off the final stage of mission 4 using only traps last night). Maneuvering through the maps without ever being spotted is incredibly satisfying, and in some missions, incredibly difficult. Progressing your accuracy from all hits, to all headshots, to all through the eye or through the ear shots (beautifully confirmed by the amazing kill-cam) feels great. Doing that to 3-4 enemies in a row, all in a single breath feels amazing. This is really some kick-ass sniping. And you can make it even more kick-ass by tweaking the difficulty in a fairly flexible way. 

The in-game collectibles are completely meaningless, getting them all doesn't confer any kind of stat bonus or unlock new equipment, but I still like finding them as it satisfies that inner OCD (especially the bottles).

The lack of a save system could be seen as a down side. It's checkpoint only. So if you screw something up, you may have to repeat a decent chunk, though they are usually pretty close together once you figure out the optimum pattern for a particular map.

One of the greatest sniping games that make you live in the atmosphere of world war 2, the sniping style is very cool and tends to be realistic at the highest difficulty and this makes the game integrated, the graphic and the sound is amazing, and the gameplay is so far so good, it deserves 9.5/10

Despite owning them I have never played through a Sniper Elite game so I decided to play through them from v2. I'm so glad I did, its a wonderful game. 

It looks much better I expected for an older game and plays exceptionally well too, except for just a couple of glitches that don't play nice with Windows 11 (specifically any ALT-TAB will probably crash the game, and I had to play around with a couple of audio codecs) But I expected something more elderly feeling and much more problematic. 

But the main gameplay mechanics are so well thought through and very satisfying. At the start of this WW2-based story I was just blasting away, not being a stealth kinda guy, but this game sure does teach you by the end how to sneak in the shadows, pick the right cover and sharpen your eye to the slightest movement to spot those bad guys. It's not an easy game, at least for me - but was very rewarding to finish. 

And then of course there is that infamous kill-cam, glorious and brutal in every way I had been led to believe. 

I'm so glad this wasn't the glorified shooting gallery I feared it would be, and so glad I gave it a try (thanks, Miller!) I've always had a soft spot for Rebellion games (mostly cos of their love for 2000AD) and now I cant wait to give no. 3 a try. Outstanding.

In Sniper Elite V2, you take the role of the worst marksman the collective allied powers could muster who is sent on a high-stakes covert mission by his superiors from within intellegence agencies to destroy progress Nazi superweapons, the V2 Rockets. You know. As a joke. To aid him, you gain access to a wide arsenal of submachineguns that your international assassin can just barely figure out which end is which on, pistols that are all broken and work improperly to some degree and high-power battle rifles with worn-out rifling, thousands and thousands of rounds of reduced power ammunition, and increasingly powerful optics made in the back of a moving truck that are incapable of any adjustment.

Coincidentally, as you undergo your mission, the magnetic field of the earth becomes much more powerful in Europe. Thousands die. This forces the people of Europe to redesign their roadways to only go in straight lines though low-magnetism areas, so there is only one path throughout all of the missions. On top of this added challenge, your projectiles (which are low velocity to avoid radar detection) are being wrestled to the earth, clawing all well-made death machines to an estimation of 3,679 Minute of Angle accuracy. To make up for this handicap, though, your infantry rifles do have anti-tank capabilities and the majority of your opponents are firing at you with fire hoses filled with lead fishing weights.

As far as the plot goes, it's your normal fare. It's a historic fiction game set between 1939 and 1945 very similar to others such as Medal of Honor, Call of Duty, etc. Now I have a bone to pick. These games all rip eachother off in their writing. Their characters all look the same, even have the same names, the games all take place at the same times in the same places. I mean, compare the main antagonist of this game, Adolf "Fuhrer" Hitler, to that of the Adolf Hitler character in any of the games I mentioned previously. What hacks. They even all have the same moustache. Is it really so hard to come up with your OWN setting? How about you call your war something other than "World War Two"? What about the first one? And why Germany? Why not something like Antagonistia or Detroit for a name? Some of the most uncreative writing I've ever found in a video game. Although, later in the game, I do like the twist where your character is bitten by a radioactive Nazi and gains x-ray vision, which reveals that the Nazis were really skeletons all along. It adds a nice twist to the setting and what I think would have actually happened were this a real war.

I would recommend this game for young readers ages 8 to 12 who are hypoglycemic, get in excess of 40 hours of sleep a day, are multilingual, and have chronic vestigial flight capabilities.

Sniper Elite V2 is Rebellion's second attempt at the sniper genre and it fails in everything except the bullet cam. The game is the re-imagining of the first game with a much better presentation, but it is uneven and inelegantly put together. With broken mechanics and linear mission layout, it felt like an overlong and boring WWII knock-off. Enemy AI is nonexistent and levels are based on trial and error in a punishing, scripted and unpolished manner. At the very rare instances in which V2 works as a sniper game, it looks like the game is working - but just barely.

Mechanics are clanky with Karl, the sniper, constantly snagging around or getting stuck altogether. Cover in this game is laughable and stiff. You get glued to a surface and can't either shoot or throw grenades until you sneak all the way to the edge, and then Karl pops out of cover - with his body completely exposed - and shoots or throws the grenade while being mauled by the enemy. While doing so, your aim is jerked to the side and off-target. Karl is also a lousy thrower and when he doesn't girly throws the grenade at his own feet, the grenade gets blocked by invisible edges and stays put beside your head.

This game is based on the idea of Karl stealthly making his way through battlefields littered with soldiers in order to find a snipping vantage point, but the environments are unsuited to the task with the paths being always straight-forward and pre-determined; with the passable terrain being limited even with better paths visible to the player. Instead, you get funneled to scripted firefights your feeble sniper is completely unsuited for. The game activelly wants the player to duke it out with massed enemies that can soak full SMG magazines to the face (all two of them) while killing Karl with a couple of aim-botted shots. Your secondary weapons are outright broken, being inaccurate to the point of being useless, leading to what should have been one-sided executions into complete fiascos. The impossibly bad gunplay forces the player to shoot his sniper rifle while holding CTRL like in a turkey shoot with enemies moving mindlessly back and forth. Given how bad combat is, it is mindbloggling why V2 forces this kind of interaction for 90% of the time.

To add insult to injury, the game is very fond of spawning enemies all around - and even to the point of spawning them literally in front of you. The game is also littered with cheap ambushes in waypoints previously cleared of enemies. With instances where the only way to survive is with the foreknowledge from a past failed attempt. Add to this the disfunctional checkpoint system and we have a punishing, tiresome mess.

The devs really didn't know what snipping is and the gunplay in this game is bloody awful. The only working mechanism - the sniping - is also bad with many desyncs during gameplay making the bullet pass through the enemies and hitting the wall behind them (but not failing to alerting everybody, of course). Enemy snipers also instantly spot you and shoot you following a time stamp, even if his rifle is pointing upwards due to his body jerking violent because you just shot him (but not fatally). One or two shots and you are dead. This is particularly annoying when you have to run the gauntlet atop roofs under the sights of an enemy "elite" sniper team that cheats and only spawns individually or in pairs when you reach their killzone. Hell, I was even killed by the sniper tiger team during a cutscene!

Stealth is outright broken and enemies see you from across the map, at night, covered by mist or walls, and hip-snipe you over 200m with a 9mm submachine gun. This completely defeats the purpose of find a high sniper nest for a vantage point, since you get headshots from a pistol-wielding enemy bellow. Your first shot will alert all enemies and a hive-mind will guide every soldier in sight to charge towards your exact location. This happens even in very dark, noisy environments such as atop an embattled anti-air tower at night. There is an attempt to ambience sounds masking your shots but this is lackluster and shallow.

There are few guns in this game, with Soviets using Lugers and MG-42 mounted machine guns. Costumes are also mediocre, with colonels and majors dressed as generals or regular grunts. Snipers' only difference is a dark overcoat, dressing like hobos. Tanks insta-spot you and are easily dispatched.

Co-Op presents some great ideas but it lacks the sophistication of its sucessor. Campaign Co-Op is good to plow through the dreadful story and Overwatch is boring. The only positives in V2 are the new voice and the sounds. Karl is now a deep-voice, gruff veteran that will become something much better in Afrika. Jerries speak German and Ruskies speak Russian. That is all.

Sniper Elite V2 is a one-trick poney, with a nice story of killing a Nazi scientist before he sells out to the Ruskies being stretched into 10 missions held together by kill-cams. Finishing this game felt like a slog and I do not look forward to doing it again. There is one single interaction with another character in the game, and only to stretch 5 missions into 10. This was clearly a missed oportunity with such an interesting story. Hell, small talk between enemies is more interesting than the overral story. Karl could, for example, befriend or even romance a female Soviet sniper and end up fighting against her at a poignant finale where he needs to accomplish his mission at all costs and stop her from taking the Nazi scientist. Thanks God we had Afrika!
Sniper Elite V2 did everything it could to make me hate it. It starts by showing you stealth, and how awesome it's bullet cam is, and teaches you how to play the game.

This game is a sad waste of potential, just like everything else that comes out of Rebellion. There's a wonderful ballistics model, and the kill-cam is really nice, but the rest of the game is an awful slog. You're given a handful of items, none of which will ever be helpful. Your silenced pistol is too inaccurate to use beyond literally a few in-game feet. If you're hiding outside a doorway and your enemy is on the other side of the room, you've got maybe a 30% chance of hitting his head. You won't want to aim anywhere else, hitting him anywhere else just sets him off. Rocks will trigger enemies, but can distract them for about a half-second. I haven't ever used them because if I'm that close and they don't know I'm there, I'd rather just shoot them with the pistol. I won't touch on the SMG, it's so inaccurate and has so little ammo that they might as well have ignored it. You're better off spamming your rifle, stunlocking with the pistol, or more likely just letting them murder you so that you can restart.

I hear rumors about things known as "stealth" and "flanking", though I've never seen them nor have I ever seen an opportunity for them to manifest. That's not a lack of skill, there's just no other path to take. The first level is within a bombed-out city, which means that there are a handful of buildings you can go in, and everything else is invisible walls and rubble. There is one path winding through the streets, and you have to walk through the open in order to get to the next objective. The first two missions might as well have been on rails for all the freedom you're given. Waypoints and invisible walls push you ever forward, you're never given any reason nor opportunity to place traps on enemies, move bodies you've shot, or otherwise use the level organically. This issue is compounded by the fact that the enemies will spawn in and re-arrange themselves spontaneously depending on your "progress". This means that you'll pretty much never be able to place TNT as traps, you can only trigger them by shooting them. In order to use it as a trap, you'd have to manually place it next to an enemy, then backtrack to a vantage point and trigger the explosives. In lieu of that you could just shoot the enemy from the vantage point and skip the middleman, or sneak up on the enemy and use the silenced pistol. However, the latter option is likely to trigger enemy rearrangements or spontaneous reinforcements as you approach. Enemies are super-eagle-eyed, so you can forget about sneaking around within 100 feet of an enemy unless they're scripted to stare away from you forever until shot. That could change as you get closer, they could spontaneously shift into a patrol route because you passed through an invisible trigger. The awareness indicator is low to the ground, hard to see, and if it's there you've pretty much already tipped them off to your location. This goes double for snipers, who spawn in only when you're about to blindly encounter them, and they are set up so that they will always immediately spot you and engage. If you manage to cheat the detection system through a combination of luck and respawn-based clairvoyance, that still makes them the first target you *have* to shoot in order to progress. On the second level, they're placed so that they can't see you, but that's only so that you can exploit the noise mechanic. The noise mechanic doesn't care about ambient sounds, there's an indicator that pops up when specific events happen (like a train horn), and during that interval you can do *anything* without drawing attention. At all other times, every spawned enemy will hear every shot, and all nearby enemies will track upright footsteps. While enemies are eagle-eyed, they are forgetful. If you're lucky no one has Line of Sight to you and you can wait the minute or so that it takes for all the enemies to assume you've given up and gone home. Be prepared to use and abuse this feature.

My suggestion is to download the demo. If you enjoyed blowing people's brains out, play the level again. That's the level right after the tutorial, copied entirely. It never gets better than that level right there. The maps are just as restrictive, the enemies spawn/rearrange spontaneously in the same "just to F*ck with you" maner, and the objectives are never more than "go here", "plant the thing" or "shoot the guy". I don't blame you for enjoying the shooting, I certainly did. There's just no reason to purchase the full game. No other part of the experience is worth the investment, if you're only there for the shooting than you might as well stick with the demo that lets you shoot stuff for free. If someone's done a Let's Play of this game from start to finish, you should just watch that and be done with it. You can't play this game any other way, the only variable would be your personal shooting performance. To simulate that, I refer you back to the demo.

Old-school game where you are a sniper in Berlin towards the end of World War II. You are an American, dropped into Berlin. Your mission is to stop the Soviets from gaining German rocket secrets. So you get to shoot Nazis, Soviets and any others that threaten your cover. Cool enough. Note: You get this title by buying the remastered version.

[b]NOTE: Mild spoilers from the end of the first Sniper Elite are present in this review.[/b]

Even though 2005's Sniper Elite was a well received hit during its heyday, it still came as a welcomed surprise when its successor was announced some eight long years later in 2012. During the interim between releases, the only dedicated sniper titles that graced the itchy trigger fingers of gamers were Sniper: Ghost Warrior in 2010, and the much less popular Sniper Art of Victory in 2008. With Sniper Elite V2, players are thrown back into the days of World War II yet again, with a slew of new missions and a brand new primary objective; stop the launch of the devastating V2 rocket.

Once again, sniping enthusiast gamers take control of Karl Fairburne; the main character from the original game, who is not only a skilled marksman, but has now become a Lieutenant for the American OSS. At the end of the first game, Karl comes across the plans for the V2 rocket, a powerful ballistic missile that threatens the entirety of the human race, and in knowing that it should come as no surprise that Sniper Elite V2 centers around this devastating force. With the ultimate goal of stopping the launch of the V2 rocket, Karl embarks on a journey through 11 missions that take place in Berlin during 1945. Since there are no dates present on the mission debriefing screens, it's impossible to tell if V2 is a slight reboot of the original title, if the dates simply overlap in some areas, or if the series of events that are presented take place immediately after the first game.

The first thing to note here is that the difficulty of the game as a whole has been reduced rather dramatically in comparison to the series' debut release; this can be seen as both a good and bad thing, depending on how spicy you like your simulations. However, that is not to say that Sniper Elite V2 is without its challenges, as some areas of the game are dreadfully difficult, especially on its highest difficulty setting. Of course, the realistic ballistics that made the franchise stand out to begin with are still included; gravity, wind speed, heart rate, breathing, stance, and distance all play an active role when using the sniper rifles. Thanks to how significantly gaming technology advanced between 2005 and 2012, the aforementioned realism factors are much more fine tuned in this sequel.

Thankfully, Karl doesn't control like he's on lubed up ice skates anymore; in fact, the controls are fantastically sturdy and well modernized. Another huge improvement to the system of the game is the inclusion of on-screen checkpoints that help guide you to your next destination, rather than having to keep switching screens to view a map. However, it is frustrating that the enemies can hear you even when you're crouching and walking slowly, and since Rebellion did away with the visibility meter from the first title, it's hard to tell just how visible you are to your foes. It's a bit of a missed opportunity that something such as close covert knife kills weren't included in this release. That can be forgiven though, thanks to the new and very interesting x-ray bullet kill cams, which show off when you shoot out an enemy's eyeball, pierce their lung, or get a direct headshot.

As far as graphics go, Sniper Elite V2 hasn't aged very much at all. The levels are beautifully decrepit and ravaged by war, there are tons of derelict buildings to hide in, loads of debris scattered about, blown up vehicles, random fires, and much more. There's also a great use of dynamic and atmospheric lighting, as well as smoke. The only areas of the game that are noticeably older are the less-than-detailed sky boxes, and the clayish look of the skin on the character models. That being said, the title still looks phenomenal while running at 144Hz with a 1080p resolution. The voice acting has also been greatly improved, though sadly the same cannot be said for the soundtrack; the latter of which seems to have taken a step back from the original release, with many of the few tracks being reused from level to level, and coming across too subtle.

While there is marginal room for improvement, Sniper Elite V2 is still one of the very best sniper simulations on the market today. Rebellion made a load of improvements over the original installment, even though they did drop the overall difficulty in a move that was to surely help attract a less hardcore crowd. The realism of the ballistics factors are better and more refined than its predecessor, and offer up a new set of challenges for those who want as real of a sniping experience as a video game can provide. When it comes to World War II, Wolfenstein has the crown for a guns blazing approach, and Sniper Elite wears the crown for stealth.

Sniper Elite V2 did everything it could to make me hate it. It starts by showing you stealth, and how awesome it's bullet cam is, and teaches you how to play the game.

Then it follows it up with a second mission that is impossible to stealth. The only thing the game shows you up to that point is stealth so you think "This game is broken." and honestly, yeah it is. The stealth in this game is broken, it's not "non existant" it's just not possible to do in the second mission (and other missions). So I put down the game because screw it. It's not fun.

About a year later I returned to Sniper Elite V2, and said "Screw it, let's just beat the game, get some achievements and never play it again." I threw the game on "Cadet" and I decide to give it one last shot.

I'm glad I did. Sniper Elite V2 is a horrible stealth game. But it's a fun "sniping" game. You don't play this game like you would play the epic Call of Duty Modern Warfare Sniping level. You instead play it like you play the rest of the call of duty levels. Yes you can stealth many parts of the game, but it takes forever and often one misstep brings everything down on you and you'll restart. Instead the minute you misstep, say "Screw it" and go out gun blazing. In fact this game has a REALLY good sniper set up. The player has quite a few tools at his disposal, the Sniping is challenging but fun, the ai does remember where they saw the player last (Which means you can move and then snipe who ever comes looking) and there is a really good level design work here.

And the kill cam. Dear god, the kill cams are amazing. For a five year old game, watching a bullet penetrate an enemy from 100 miles away in a unique way every time is weirdly glorious. The bullet travels, the air manipulated around it until it penetrates (And yes penetrates is the right word) into a body, moving through vital organs until it exits. It's a glorious moment and while it's over done a bit, it's exciting at least 75 percent of the time, and probably closer to 100. It's just an absolute exciting experience especially when you pull off that 400 meter shot, or you successfully nail the perfect shot.

So does it make it a good game. Well that depends. It's not a great military shooter, but it is a VERY fun sniping game. I really prefer it on the easier difficulty, and the game feels broken once in a while, or unfair. But the game makes up for it in visuals, and that feeling when each mission's plan comes together. It COULD be better, and it's not perfect, but it's worth a play. I don't know if I'd pay the full 20 bucks for it, but for 10 bucks or less it's easily worth the money and time to play through it.

As for the game, it still holds up to this day. Compared to new Sniper Elites that are larger open areas, this one is more of a linear corridor style. Graphics are still very good. Visually a great game, but besides the initial fun of setting up the shot and seeing the bullet cam the fun kind of drops off. It gets repetitive and in some cases makes the game hard to play as a sniper. You get in to close quarter fights that you can only really survive by pulling out the pistol or machine gun to complete. And it amazes me that every single enemy in the area instantly knows exactly where you are once you fire a shot. In an urban setting with buildings, streets and walls, the sounds of gunfire would echo and be pretty difficult to pinpoint.

Straight up: this is not a tactical game about sniping, and definitely not realistic. If you want a very arcade-like shooter then maybe go for it based on its one big draw: slow-mo bullet cam. I have played the game for hours just for this feature, but once it wears off you are left with flawed and rough game mechanics and plot. Plot is bad, but not critically so, I've seen worse. The gameplay features firefights mainly at under 200m with very unrealistic features (such as shooting through corners due to bullet tracing form the crosshair rather than the gun, and using 3rd person to peek and scout the area). The actual situations it places you in as a sniper are also poorly chosen, as most snipers excel in situations of patience, strategy and long-range targets. Forget all of that; it is very linear and confined, and you have will be just as good firing quick snapshots between sprints as you would if you crawled to a good spot, steadied your heartbeat, controlled your breathing and took a good shot. Additionally you just shrug off bullets call of duty style.

The campaign quickly becomes boring and repetitive, and the multiplayer in my experience has many hackers (Or possibly lag from most players living around Russia). On one occasion, I put a full round of MP40 ammo into another player in deathmatch, and they proceeded to snipe me at point blank without being scoped in. The only real way to have fun is to get a few friends who all have the game and play around on a closed server, which then becomes great fun. On a similar note, playing the co-op with a friend also increases the amount of entertainment exponentially by having you focus more on having a good time over just playing the game by itself. However, the game by itself is repetitive, boring, and in case of the multiplayer, frustrating.

The first 'Sniper Elite' titled game from Rebellion was disgustingly bad. It was pretentious, sure, and it created some vile fan community... But it was awful all over. Yet, it was upgraded, and it evolved into something better! 'Sniper Elite' V2 isn't a horrendous game, like V1. Now it's just silly. Sure, there is some 'unique' charm, made by a combination of intrusive usage of sniper rifles, with kinda tricky 'almost realistic' ballistic part, and slow-mo 'x-ray bullet cam' effect. Which is literally provokes people to make shot after shot, again and again, and see another dummy's brain or testicles splattered. But, again, all over it's just another silly game about World War II made by people who know nothing about it and don't give a shoot about it. And made for people alike, with carefully cultivated by the gaming industry bad taste for lame on-rail scripted shooters.

What were the worst points in the Sniper V1? By gameplay terms, in the first place, the shooting was bad. All the weaponry in hands of the player besides the main rifle was nerfed up to no use. V2 saved that feature, as one of its own personality markings, but still, other guns now are slightly more useful. To the point when I'm able to do some room cleaning without a long and clumsy scoped boomstick. Not good enough, yeah, but way better than it was.

Next, the AI. Now, the enemies are learned to take covers, and even walk around corners from different sides! Sure, they're still dummies, blindly running forward on your position, even on the hardest difficulty setting. Eagle-eyed snipers, who can peek you from a great distance in one place, but will neglect your presence in close-combat range, are also there. The "stealth" part is also spoiled from the start to the end of the game - you'll never need that, anyway. Except for two optional achievements, in the DLCs 'St.Pierre' and 'Neudorf Outpost'. But, but, all in all, AI is surely much more complicated than in the V1, and has some fairplay tricks to make you feel oppressed, at least in some moments. A respawning-stormtroopers-on-your-back cliche is still widely in use, sure. But now you can make some traps on your way, which seems kinda useful in some dire situations where you're supposed to hold the point for some time against hordes of enemies. That part was even kinda hilarious. But not all that useful, alas!

The other bad part of Sniper V1 was about the level maps. There were about 5 of them for 28 'missions'... And they were poorly made, for the most part. Except maybe, occasionally, there was a place to perform a shot for more than 300 meters range. In the Sniper V2, there are 10 maps for 11 game missions (+some DLC's, each is 1 new map for 1 new mission, usually). Each map in the V2 is usually covered in half of an hour... Yeah, the maps are That Short. They're looking not bad overall, but it's all the same - narrow corridor, with the ability to walk around some house from one side or another, at most. So, the marketing passages about 'Sniper's choice' and 'using the Environment' are about the 'hide behind the chest-high wall and squeeze the trigger as you please'. Since the maps are quite short, I doubt that many players will ever achieve a range above 350-400 meters (except the very last shot of the game, which is not skill-based, by all means).

Finally, the story and the player's motivation. In the first game, the player was an American agent in '45 Berlin, dressed as a German paramilitary, and killing Soviet soldiers before they dig up some really dirty nazi secrets. In the second game, the scenario is slightly more evasive. Now, the Russians are not the targets just because they are Russians and Commies, and whatever. No, they're planning to shoot the V2 rocket, armed with some nerve gas from Berlin, straight to London (3 times V2's actual range) and pretend it was Nazis! And actual Nazies who made the rockets and the gas - are helping the Soviets with the attack! To make Germany's reparations even higher, supposedly. Yeah, I guess people who've bought CoD Black Ops will buy any kind of crud, coming as a "history-based scenario". Why do the Soviets bomb their Allies? Because that's what evil tyrants like Stalin always do, right? Or not? Oh, who cares! Just pop more heads and see their brains explode, that's what this game is about!

Before I set my mark, I'll say a few words about multiplayer there. It is always a room full of campers, isn't that great? Well, I know some good shooters where some maps are made for this kind of self-entertainment... But to make all the multiplayer around campers is surely an extreme way of thinking. Even the fact that ballistic there, with bullet derivation and all that, in reality, looks quite arcade and dumbed down... Well, as I said from the beginning, the game is silly and stupid. And better than the first one. And aimed at some blood-thirsty 13-years-old maniacs who're not caring about whom to shoot, or why.

Mark is 6/10. And downvote, for it's all still not fun enough.

Thankfully, "Sniper Elite V2" is a FAR better game than Sniper Elite" (the first game in the series).  The developers fixed all my major complaints with that earlier work.  In fact, the only complaints I've got about this game are:

- Enemies spawn in areas as you cross certain points.  You can spend all the time in the world clearing everything out, take one step, and have a whole new batch of enemies appear in the very same areas you just cleared out.  That's a tad annoying.
- In several cases, the newly spawned enemies will default to having seen you (even if you're totally hidden).
- If you're an Achievement hound, there's an Achievement for finding all the bottles and all the gold bars in the game.  The problem is that the bottles are just plain old brown beer/wine bottles in areas consisting mostly of rubble, and the gold bars are practically identical to all the bricks lying around those rubble-strewn areas (except for the fact that they gleam with light).

Normally, I write these reviews after I complete all the Achievements in a game.  But, since there are a lot of co-op Achievements here, I'm doing it now after having finished the base game and a few Achievements here and there.  It took me 21.3 hours to do that.  You'll see some reviews here where people claim they finished the game in 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, etc. hours (those are ones I found).  I say horse-puckey.  Maybe they grabbed their SMG and ran through the thing like they were playing Doom.  But, this is a sniper game where the whole point is to kill enemies from a distance and not be seen while doing it.  So, don't worry about not getting your money's worth.  The game is very well done and even a single run-through will be worth it even at my miserly dollar per hour metric.

UPDATE:  It took me another 16.7 hours (for a total of 38.0 hours) to finish the base game with all Achievements completed.  Definitely worth the money (though it looks like it goes on sale for 5 or 6 dollars every 3 or 4 months).

This is not a stealth game.  It is an action game masquerading as a stealth game.  The problem is that it is not a good action game.  NONE (read: ZERO-ZILCH-NADA) of the mechanics support fast-paced, action game-play.  The only weapon accurate beyond spitting distance is the sniper rifle, but with the attached scope, it is much too hard to maintain situational awareness and to transition from one target to another.

This game routinely spawns enemies behind you, in places you've already cleared, and in inaccessible locations to force you into a gun-fight, removing the player's actions and decisions from the game-play loop.  It doesn't matter if you play well.  It doesn't matter if you're a good shot.  It doesn't matter if you are stealthy.  NOTHING YOU DO MATTERS.  The game will simply spawn enemies to FORCE YOU OUT OF STEALTH.

On the harder difficulties, enemies can track you through walls and do not need to see you to know where you are.  You cannot hide in buildings or try to move from concealment-to-concealment, whether or not they can see you is irrelevant.  They will know where you've gone and they will shoot you if you try to peak out.

The main problem with this game is that someone decided their script was too good to allow the player to mess it up.  They wanted this section to be a big gun battle, so it's a big gun battle, regardless of the player's actions.  They wanted this target to die in this one way, so the guy dies in the one way.  The player can't explore around.  The player can't find alternative ways of killing the target.  The player is not allowed to make choices.

This stands in stark contrast to later games in the franchise, and is a shame.  I can honestly tell you that I don't know what the story is because I lost all attachment to it after being forcibly removed from stealth through no fault of mine for the fourth time.

If this game is on a deep (read: less than one dollar) sale, it might be worth it, but please don't pay an entire dollar to play this game.

Sniper Elite 2 offers a thrilling World War II sniper experience, placing players in the shoes of an elite marksman behind enemy lines. With its realistic ballistics and tense stealth gameplay, it delivers intense and satisfying sniper encounters. The game's detailed environments and X-ray kill cam add to the immersion, highlighting the gruesome results of well-placed shots. Despite some repetitive missions and limited enemy AI, its focus on precision shooting and strategic decision-making keeps players engaged throughout. Sniper Elite 2 is a must-play for fans of tactical shooters, offering a visceral and immersive sniper experience amidst the chaos of war.

“Sniper Elite V2” is a game that puts you in the shoes of an American sniper behind enemy lines during the final days of World War II. The game’s campaign is set in Berlin in 1945, and your mission is to ensure that the German scientists behind the V2 rocket program meet a bullet before the Russians can capture them.

The game is known for its detailed sniping mechanics and the satisfaction derived from executing well-planned strategies. You can lay traps for enemy soldiers, use their screams of pain to attract more targets, and change positions to create confusion. The game also features a kill-cam that provides a slow-motion, X-ray view of your successful shots.

However, the game’s level design can be inconsistent. While some levels offer large open courtyards that allow for strategic gameplay, others involve tight corridors or narrow paths where enemy soldiers can easily spot you. In these situations, the game can devolve into a pop-up shooting gallery.

Despite these shortcomings, “Sniper Elite V2” offers a unique experience that sets it apart from typical World War II shooters. The game captures the essence of what it means to be a sniper and provides a variety of tactical opportunities for assassination and covert operations.

Overall, “Sniper Elite V2” is a fun and engaging game, especially if you’re into the genre or the franchise. It may have a few clunky aspects, but its focus on sniping gameplay and the thrill of executing carefully planned strategies make it a worthwhile experience.

Hey kiddo, Handsome Jack here... and I just played Sniper Elite V2, and apparently this is what happens when you take World War II, remove all the subtlety, and hand one extremely patient man a rifle with a direct line to the human skeleton. Fantastic. Finally, a game with a clear business model.

You play as Karl Fairburne, a man whose entire personality seems to be “find a high building, lie down, and ruin someone's day from several hundred meters away.” And honestly, I respect the commitment. You sneak through the ruins of Berlin, hunt Nazis, sabotage weapons, and generally make yourself a one-man corporate restructuring department.

The best part is obviously the X-ray kill cam. You fire a bullet, the game freezes, and suddenly we're getting a full medical presentation on exactly which organs you've just ruined. Skull? Crushed. Spine? Gone. Lungs? Having a very bad afternoon. At some point I stopped feeling like a sniper and started feeling like a particularly enthusiastic radiologist.

The stealth is pretty basic, but that's okay. You find a good position, wait for the right moment, use environmental noise to cover your shot, and pull the trigger. When everything goes perfectly, you feel like the greatest marksman who ever lived.

Then you miss.

ONE.

And suddenly every Nazi in Berlin has apparently received a company-wide email containing your exact location.

Now you're sprinting through a ruined building while twenty soldiers shoot at you, wondering where your career went wrong.

Beautiful.

The game definitely shows its age. The environments aren't as open as the newer games, the AI can be questionable, and the mechanics are much simpler. But there's something charming about it. It knows exactly what it wants to be. Sneak around, line up ridiculous shots, kill Nazis, watch their skeletons explode in slow motion, repeat.

And honestly, sometimes that's all you need.

It's not as polished as Sniper Elite 3, 4, or 5, but the foundation is right here. This is where the series really established its identity, and you can see why the formula stuck around.

8/10, kiddo.

Fresh from completing Sniper Elive V2, I thought I'd give a brief couple of points on the game.

Positives:
+WWII setting.  Differentiates itself from the current 'modern' trend.  Appreciate WWII was the big thing 5-10 years ago.
+Graphics.  Decent graphics, some nice effects like fire and explosions that look good without too much scrutiny.
+Physics.  Completed on Sniper Elite difficulty so got to experience some decent bullet drop balistics etc.  Shots are definitely missable if you're not careful.
+X-Ray Kill Cam.  This just never gets old.  Ever.  There's something immensely satisfying seeing the skeleton of your enemy shatter into little bits.
+Campaign length.  Though it could be completed quicker (I'm sure), I got a good 10+ hours out of the single player.

Negatives:
-A.I.  Far too easy.  The game can effectively be progressed by simply giving your position away, letting the A.I. run around in the open as they try to hit you.  Makes sniping actually a little too easy.
-Opernplatz.  There's a progression bug on this map. I hit it, couldn't get past and ended up shelving the game for 6-12 months.  Thankfully, a fresh download seemed to let me move on when I finally returned.  Very disappointing.
-Story.  Generic America saves the world (well, America saves London in this instance).  Not very exciting and a little too Hollywood.
-Linearity.  Maps can be moved across using various routes but it's essentially a point A to point B fare.  Shame really. 
-Kit too situational.  I had mines, trip mines, dynamite, grenades and a rock (no, NOT  Dwayne Johnson) but using them was VERY situational.  Had the game given me better A.I. (i.e. supressing and flanking etc.) then maybe I'd have used a more tactical approach such as trip mining doorways and the like - but the game just doesn't need it.  You can treat it like any other shooter and progress just fine.  A massively missed opportunity. 

Overall, I'd definitely say I had fun with Sniper Elite V2 (taking aside Opernplatz) and would recommend it as being 'worth playing'.  Arguably one of the better sniping games in recent years.

Lastly, it's really cheeky of Rebellion to peddle DLC and the next game on the exit screen.  Bad form, folks.

Tip for the rocket mission: There are a lot of enemies after you kill the supervisor. The game suddenly told me I failed the mission, I restarted the checkpoint 2 more times and could not figure out why it wasn't letting me fight the enemies. That's when I had enough and went to google. If the game tells you that you failed, then you restart the checkpoint but it gives you a few seconds before it tells you failed again. It is not a bug, you have to now shot the fuel tank on the rocket. It's a glowing red circle. I thought it was glitching for me since it wouldn't let me fight the enemies. (Sorry that was a long explain, but hopefully it helps anyone that's going to play this game or is stuck on this mission).
